name: Egg and wine diet

card.summary: A three-day crash plan of eggs, dry white wine, steak and black coffee, used for quick slimming before an event.
card.note: Very low in fiber and micronutrients and built around a bottle of wine a day; weight lost is largely water.

quick.overview:
The egg and wine diet is a three-day fad plan of eggs, dry white wine, grilled steak and black coffee. People have used it for rapid slimming, for example before an occasion, so the body looks leaner.

Grokipedia traces it to Helen Gurley Brown's 1962 book Sex and the Single Girl, with a reprint in Vogue in 1977, and describes roughly 1,100 kcal a day [1].
quick.how: As described, each day repeats the same pattern: eggs and wine at breakfast and lunch, then a small grilled steak at dinner with the rest of the wine, with unlimited black coffee. It is meant to last three days only.
quick.risks: The plan excludes fruit, vegetables and grains and relies on alcohol for part of its calories. Commentary summarised on Grokipedia says early weight loss is mostly water and that dehydration and regain are likely [1].

lead: The egg and wine diet is a short, restrictive eating plan in which a person eats eggs, grilled steak and black coffee and drinks a bottle of dry white wine over three days. Its purpose is quick slimming, so people look leaner for a specific occasion [1].

Grokipedia attributes the plan to Helen Gurley Brown, who published it in Sex and the Single Girl in 1962 as a weekend fix, and says Vogue reprinted it in 1977 as a three-day plan [1]. Wikipedia confirms the book was a long-running bestseller that inspired a 1964 film [2].

Nutrition commentary summarised there notes that the plan is high in protein but offers almost no fiber or varied micronutrients, and that the weight lost is largely water [1]. Forum mentions, such as T Nation's diet threads, deal with other low-carbohydrate and lean-physique plans rather than this one.

chain: Three days of very low carbohydrate, calorie-restricted eating
angle.text: The diet is used for a fast, short-term slimming effect before an event. The visible change comes from a calorie deficit and fluid loss rather than lasting fat change.

infobox: Eggs, steak, dry white wine, black coffee

paras: Per the Grokipedia summary, a typical day is one egg and a glass of wine with black coffee at breakfast, two eggs and two glasses of wine at lunch, and 150 g of grilled steak with the remaining wine at dinner [1]. Eggs are boiled or poached without added fat, and the steak is seasoned only with pepper and lemon [1].

The plan is credited to Helen Gurley Brown, whose Sex and the Single Girl appeared in 1962 [1]. The book sold well internationally and spawned a 1964 film [2]. A 1977 Vogue reprint widened its audience, within a period of many celebrity-promoted fad diets [1].

The summary says the plan lacks fiber, complex carbohydrates and varied micronutrients, and that rebound gain after it is typical because the early loss is mostly water [1]. Regimens centred on large quantities of alcohol also raise the usual cautions about alcohol intake.
